unit: WF4 Distil Sources registry provenance, content alignment and heading-anchored excerpting
description: Registry order "P2 reversed": four sources fetched in this registry order must each keep their own url, title, source_id and excerpt.
why_it_exists: Execution 329 (a real matter): every Sources row was written with the WRONG URL against its own title and excerpt, pairwise swapped. The url was resolved as `j.url || (ctx.urls || [])[i]`; Fetch Source runs with fullResponse: true and returns only data, headers, statusCode and statusMessage, so there is never a j.url and the positional fallback always won - and ctx.urls is a legacy list built by Build Draft Context in a DIFFERENT order from the Source Registry that actually drove the fetches. The result was a citation whose link points at a different Act: fabricated authority wearing a correct-looking title. The fallback was deleted and replaced by two independent controls, n8n pairedItem provenance and a declared-phrase content check. ctx.urls in this fixture is deliberately WRONG and deliberately in a different order from the registry, so if the deleted positional fallback ever comes back it puts a different Act URL on every row and these assertions fail.

assertions: exactly four source rows with four unique source_id values
source_id follows the REGISTRY position, not the response arrival position: SRC-PERM-000-01 .. -04
each row title equals its registry cite
each stored url and requested_url equals the registry url that drove that fetch
each STORED excerpt contains the want phrase of that same registry entry
all four verification_status values are RETRIEVED
each row carries a non-empty anchor_heading and excerpt_is_anchored is true
each pinpoint matches /^s \d/ - it names the anchored section, not a cross-reference
alignment_all_ok and excerpts_all_anchored are both true
no ctx.urls value appears as a stored url unless the registry asked for it
